messages:
maya: noticing a jump in inference 5xxs and tail latency for customers routed to us-east-1a. dashboards show egress path latency increase and packet loss on a subset of G5 instances. opening thread so oncall can triage.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • id: INF-2026-223987 • severity: P2 • paged: @maya @ravi • runbook: /runbooks/network-egress-deg.json
maya: metric snippets: 95th latency to model endpoints (tokens/sec) up from 180ms -> 1.2s, error rate +5% over 10m. Cloud provider metrics show packet loss spikes on enis attached to g5. Metrics: 
```
net.packet_loss.p95=5-12% (instances: i-0a123, i-0b456, i-0c789)
net.egress_latency.avg=850ms -> 1.1s
```
ravi: on it. checking VPC flow logs and AZ egress path. if this is NIC-level we might see ENI resets or host link saturation. maya, can you confirm which capacity pool these instances are in?
maya: pool=dedicated-g5-us-east-1a-prod, node group tag=redwood-infer-g5-a. customer-facing traffic skewed by DNS weights right now (we still have ~55% to this AZ).
lucas: I'm seeing repeated TCP retransmits and some connection teardown logs in the app side, KVCACHE stalls for certain model shards. sample log: 
```
2026-03-14T23:09:12Z inf-runtime shard=3 conn=12 state=kv_miss stall_ms=4200
2026-03-14T23:09:14Z net kern: ENI-reset dev=eni-0abc reason=driver-rx-ovf
```
anya: support getting a few customer tickets now — reports of slow responses and occasional 502s. one large customer reports batch jobs timing out. flagging SLO/PG impacts.
ravi: plan: 1) shift DNS weight away from us-east-1a to b/c (adjust at traffic-router) 2) spin up extra nodes in us-east-1b/c and move canary traffic 3) drain affected nodes and mark for host inspection 4) enable fallback model-variant on slower path for high-priority customers. executing step 1 now.
ravi: running traffic-router adjust: 
```
# shift 40% of traffic off 1a to 1b/1c
curl -X POST https://traffic-router.local/api/weights 
  -d '{"az":"us-east-1a","delta":-0.4}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
infra-bot: ADJUSTMENT OK • weights changed: us-east-1a 15% -> 10% -> now 12% after smoothing • backed off immediate cut to avoid cache thrash.
maya: seeing immediate improvement in error rate (down ~1.8%) but latency still elevated for existing connections. KV cache misses are causing extra tail. preparing to drain nodes after warmup.
lucas: starting node drain on two worst hosts: i-0a123 i-0b456. commands: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `asg detach-instances` for safe reprovisioning.
ravi: noticed DNS TTLs are 60s — we should lower to 10s for faster steering in these events. making change now, but watch for DNS resolver amplification.
maya: lowering TTL to 10s (deployed), also started routing policy fallback: prefer cross-AZ endpoints for new flows.
incident-bot: PAGER NOTE • paged lucas at 23:15 UTC for takeover.
lucas: taking over oncall. summary for incoming: egress path in us-east-1a seeing NIC-level drops -> causes KV cache stall -> increases inference latency and 5xx. mitigation in flight: DNS weight shift, node drains, extra capacity in 1b/1c. I'll coordinate post-drain testing.
anya: flagged top 10 affected customers and notified SEs. queued mitigation emails for high-traffic tenants.
lucas: after drains, we see connection churn while caches rehydrate. mitigated by seeding KV with hot-prefixes: `kv-sync --prefixes hot_prompts --targets us-east-1b,us-east-1c` — this reduced tail latency for critical flows.
```
KV WARMUP: seeded 42k keys, throughput 1500 keys/s
```
ravi: cloud provider notified — ticket open with them investigating host NIC telemetry. earlier they reported a driver bug on similar host families; requested host-level repro and NIC snapshots.
maya: customer impact summary to append to incident: ~3% of production inference traffic saw >=2s tail latency; ~0.8% faced transient 502s between 23:08-23:30 UTC. Affected customers: batch jobs and low-RPS streaming pipelines.
lucas: stabilizing. marking incident as mitigated at 23:25 UTC. leaving nodes cordoned for deeper inspection and repro offline.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • INF-2026-223987 • status: mitigated • mitigated_at: 2239876725 • responders: maya, ravi, lucas, anya • next: postmortem scheduled.
maya: handing off to eng-runtime for postmortem and long-term fix (sticky routing, host kernel upgrade). assigning lucas as owner for the postmortem doc.
lucas: will run postmortem and include action items: (1) lower DNS TTLs in runtime for failover windows (2) automated weight-shift playbook (3) probe agent on hosts to proactively detect ENI errors (4) scale warmup for KV cache during drain.
anya: support follow-up: customer comms draft ready, send after postmortem.
ravi: closing this chat — monitoring for 1h then close incident channel. thanks all for fast turnaround :thumbsup:
